resale_co.name: Residential Resale Certificate / Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), issued as a Certificate of Zoning Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Norwood Construction Office (Construction Code Official / Zoning Officer)
requirements: Inspection showing no zoning infractions and compliance with the Zoning Ordinance for continued occupancy
General inspection of the visible parts of the building for imminent hazards
Existing property inventory (basement, first floor, second floor, other)
Smoke detector and carbon monoxide detector compliance certified on the same form
Smoke detectors on each level including the basement, in each bedroom and outside the bedrooms; 10-year sealed battery or interconnected system
Carbon monoxide detectors outside the bedroom doors (battery, plug-in or combination)

fees.label: Residential Resale Certificate (CCO), including smoke and CO detector compliance
fees.quote: The fee for a Residential Resale Certificate (CCO) is $150.00

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Residential Resale Application from the Construction/Code Enforcement Forms/Applications page, fill it out and pay $150.00 by check or money order only, payable to the Borough of Norwood. Submit to the Norwood Construction Office, 455 Broadway, Norwood, NJ 07648 (201-767-7420).
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official / Building Subcode Official and Zoning Officer

evidence.quote: Any change in use, ownership, or occupancy of an existing building or structure shall require approval of a certificate of continued occupancy by the Construction Code Official.

No certificate of continued occupancy may be issued as to a residential building or any portion thereof unless approved smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, and carbon monoxide detectors have been installed as required by applicable state statute and local ordinances.
Payable By Check or Money Order ONLY

resale_co.notes: The Borough code (Chapter on Certificates of Continued Occupancy, Ord. No. 07:10) still lists $100 for the application and initial inspection and $25 per reinspection, but the Borough's current Residential Resale Application says the fee is $150.00 as of August 26, 2025, so the newer form fee is listed. The fee sheet and checklist pages of the application PDF have a text layer; the first page (Certificate of Zoning Compliance) is an image, so its wording was read visually. The construction fee code also lists "CO fee residential $100.00", which appears to be for new construction COs. Gino Tessaro's name comes from the mailto link on the department page. Annual rental registration is a rental-only program and not a resale requirement.

requirements: Smoke detectors on each level including the basement, in each bedroom, and outside and near all bedroom doors (the form says within 10 feet; the checklist says within 21 feet)
Smoke detectors must be 10-year sealed battery or an interconnected system; not in the attic, crawl spaces or immediate kitchen area
Carbon monoxide detectors outside and near all bedroom doors; battery, plug-in or combination smoke/CO type

authorities.how_to_apply: Covered by the Residential Resale Application ($150.00, check or money order only) filed with the Construction Office, 455 Broadway.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Subcode Official (Borough page); Fire Official (state directory)

evidence.quote: In the case of change of occupancy of any building subject to the requirements of §127-9 of this chapter, no owner shall sell, lease or otherwise permit occupancy for residential purposes of that building without first obtaining from the Norwood Construction Department a certificate evidencing compliance with the requirements of this chapter and N.J.S.A. 52:27D-198.1 and 52:27D-198.2.
Smoke Detector, Carbon Monoxide Detector Checklist for Residential Compliance
Smoke detectors shall be 10 yr. sealed battery-operated or an interconnected system.

fire_cert.notes: Borough Code Section 127-10 (amended 8-20-2025 by Ord. No. 2025:10) sends the smoke/CO certificate for sales to the Norwood Construction Department, and the Borough's resale application combines it with the CCO for one $150.00 fee. The code still lets the Fire Official buy and install required smoke detectors for $40 each. The 2007 CCO chapter still mentions fire extinguishers, but the current checklist (updated 08/25) lists only smoke and CO detectors, consistent with P.L.2025, c.19.

open_questions: What lead time does the Construction Office need before closing, and how long is the certificate valid?
Is there a reinspection fee under the 2025 fee change (the old code said $25)?
Bedroom-door distance for detectors: the form says within 10 feet but the checklist says within 21 feet; which does the inspector apply?
